teaser.text: ONEOK is a midstream energy company: it runs the pipes, plants, terminals and storage between producers and the businesses that use energy. Its business is to make raw production usable, move it to the right market and store it until customers need it.

stock.title: ONEOK stock forecast
stock.meta_description: ONEOK's forecast weighs bear, base and bull cases against cash flow, debt, operating execution and today's valuation.
stock.opening: ONEOK's weighted forecast reaches $144.03 in October 2029. It hinges on EBITDA growth reaching earnings and real free cash flow per share after debt costs, dilution and Apollo’s claim.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains ONEOK’s business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: Where could ONEOK's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast puts ONEOK’s weighted share price at $116.79 in October 2027. That implies a 30% total return with dividends. It reaches $128.61 in October 2028, implying a 47% total return. By October 2029, the weighted price is $144.03, implying a 68% total return.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for ONEOK?

paragraphs.text: The bear path starts at $7,900 million and reaches $8,300 million. It reflects weaker volumes, delayed projects and integration costs. The bull path starts at $9,000 million and reaches $10,498 million. It assumes stronger connections, recurring synergies and timely project starts. Throughput rose 7% in the latest quarter, but NGL EBITDA fell from $673 million to $659 million, showing why higher volumes do not guarantee higher segment earnings.

blocks.heading: How much cash does ONEOK really make?

paragraphs.text: Profit can arrive before customers pay, and cash can move into inventory or receivables before it appears in earnings. Free cash flow means cash from operations less capital spending. “Real free cash flow” goes further by subtracting stock pay, because compensation delivered in shares can dilute existing owners.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for ONEOK today?

paragraphs.text: Start with the P/E ratio, which compares the share price with annual profit. It is easy to read, but profit includes depreciation and amortization, the accounting cost of using pipelines and plants over time. In 2025, depreciation and amortization was $1.514 billion. Profit also reflects acquisition accounting, so P/E needs a cash-flow check.

blocks.heading: How much does ONEOK pay shareholders?

paragraphs.subsection: 3.5 — Debt, equity dilution and capital allocation after M&A
paragraphs.text: ONEOK also authorized up to $2 billion of share repurchases and raised its quarterly dividend to $1.07 in January 2026. Those payments can reward shareholders, but they compete with debt reduction and construction when payouts exceed free cash flow. Comparable midstream companies had a median debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 3.4x in 2025, giving investors a reference point for the burden ONEOK must manage.

blocks.heading: Is ONEOK’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Cash is the stricter test. In 2025, operating cash flow was $5.599 billion and capital expenditures were $3.152 billion. That simple difference was less than the $2.6 billion dividend, so the definition of free cash flow matters. Maintenance spending keeps existing assets safe; growth spending adds capacity. Both consume cash today.

paragraphs.text: Management guided to 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $8.2–$8.5 billion. It guided to total capital expenditures of $2.7–$3.2 billion. Its diluted EPS range is $5.38–$5.99, alongside a 3%–4% annual dividend-growth target. Management targets 3.25x debt-to-EBITDA leverage for 2027.

Dividends grow from $4.37 to $4.64 per share in the base case. The bear case falls from $4.28 to $3.85 after a cut. The bull case rises from $4.41 to $4.76. Base growth follows the low end of management’s 3%–4% target, while the downside reflects dividends exceeding free cash flow in 2025 and a reported 2026 funding gap.

earnings.opening: ONEOK's next results are expected on October 27, 2026. For ONEOK, watch whether third-quarter results support the higher annual outlook.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains ONEOK's business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: After stronger volumes and better marketing and optimization earnings, management raised its 2026 guidance for a second time on August 3. It now expects adjusted EBITDA—earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization—of $8.2–$8.5 billion. It kept total capital spending at $2.7–$3.2 billion. Its diluted earnings-per-share range is $5.38–$5.99.

Revenue rose year over year while gross margin fell, because commodity sales bring corresponding costs. Operating income and net income still improved, so the quarter was stronger overall, but the margin contraction limits what can be inferred from sales growth alone.

blocks.heading: What should ONEOK watchers look for next?

paragraphs.text: The next earnings call is scheduled for October 28, 2026. It should show whether the third quarter supports the higher annual outlook and whether second-half capital spending is moving toward the upper end of guidance. Over a longer period, investors should watch Medford, Bighorn, Texas City and Eiger. Delays would postpone customer fees while construction cash continues to leave the business.

paragraphs.subsection: 7.6 — Asset reliability, safety and ability to keep operating
paragraphs.text: Maintenance capital keeps existing facilities safe and operating; growth capital adds capacity. ONEOK guided to $550–$600 million of maintenance capital for 2026. It had spent $229 million by midyear. The distinction matters because growth can raise future earnings, but maintenance prevents today’s network from failing.
